title: MFA hardening: hash backup codes + DB code store
goal: Deliver deterministic, persistent, rate-limited MFA backup and verification-code behavior that remains correct across deploys and replays

in: MFA backup-code hashing and one-time redemption
Authoritative additive verification-code schema, server-only repository, RLS/ACL boundary, and deterministic focused verification
out: Hosted migration application, destructive reset/replay, and production changes
Canonical database type regeneration before the migration is staged

acceptance_criteria: Backup codes are cryptographically hashed and redeemed exactly once using production-safe timing
Verification codes use the approved server-only database store and survive process restarts and deploys
Expiry, attempt limits, rate limits, replay prevention, user scoping, and cleanup behavior have deterministic tests
Focused MFA tests complete without timing flakes and the account lifecycle staging suite passes

progress.summary: Implemented the authoritative additive MFA verification-code schema and wired the production MFA singleton to a server-only Supabase repository. Codes are bcrypt-hashed before persistence; service-role-only atomic RPCs enforce issue limits, user scoping, expiry, three-attempt lockout, replay prevention, revocation, and retention-aware cleanup behind an RLS/default-deny table boundary.
completed: Replaced the djb2 backup-code hash with bcryptjs hashing at cost factor 12.
Changed backup-code verification to compare against stored bcrypt hashes and conditionally mark a matching unused row as used.
Added focused tests covering bcrypt storage, successful redemption, and one-time use.
Replaced process-local verification-code storage with an explicit repository contract and fail-closed production default.
Added deterministic verification-code contract tests covering scope, expiry, lockout, replay, cooldown, and issuance limits.
Removed insecure Math.random SMS/challenge generation and verification-code logging.
Created the forward-only mfa_verification_codes migration through the Supabase CLI with RLS/default-deny grants and service-role-only atomic functions.
Wired the production singleton to the server-only Supabase repository; plaintext verification codes never reach Postgres.
Added repository, migration-contract, security-probe, migration-manifest, and hosted-ledger evidence.
